Ecto is part of 9 of my public repositories, from 2017 to 2026.

What it was for: [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (3), [AI engineering](@/projects/ai.md) (2), [Web](@/projects/web.md) (2) and [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (1).

Most recently: [Crisis map](@/work/crisis-map.md): Reports geocoded through a local Nominatim, stored as PostGIS geography and served from one capability registry: LiveView, REST, OpenAPI, MCP and CLI; [the-psycho](@/work/the-psycho.md); [llm](@/work/llm.md): Local-first, provider-agnostic archive of AI conversations (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Codex) — immutable, content-addressed, searchable evidence layer built in Elixir/Ecto.

1 of these projects runs as a live site.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses Ecto: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links Ecto to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
